prose: Pay-per-Crawl went from a WordPress plugin to ten stacks in a day: the same gate now runs on WordPress, Drupal, Laravel, Next.js, Node, Cloudflare, nginx, Caddy, Traefik and Python, published on npm, PyPI, Packagist and drupal.org. Behavior is identical everywhere: humans and reverse-DNS-verified search engines read free, while AI crawlers and scripts get an HTTP 402 with an x402 v2 header and must pay USDC on Base before the page is served.

The owner keeps 100% of payments, direct to their wallet - no custody, no ForgeMesh account, no API key. Every edition ships the same 85-agent crawler catalog and serves discovery files (/.well-known/x402.json, llms.txt, agents.txt), and each was validated with real $0.01 settlements on Base mainnet before release.
highlights: Pay-per-Crawl now runs on 10 stacks from WordPress to nginx
AI crawlers get HTTP 402 with x402 v2; humans and verified search engines free
Payment in USDC on Base before the page is served
Site owner keeps 100%, direct to wallet, no custody or API key
Shared 85-agent crawler catalog plus x402.json, llms.txt, agents.txt
Each edition validated with real $0.01 mainnet settlements
